html:
Short answer: digital signage is a network of screens showing content you control, such as menus, queues, promotions, wayfinding or staff news. A good system uses commercial-grade screens built for long daily hours, a media player, and simple content management.

Common uses

  • Retail and malls: promotions, prices, video walls.
  • Banks: queue information, rates and products.
  • Hospitals: patient information and wayfinding.
  • Hotels and restaurants: menus, events and directions.
  • Offices and schools: internal news, schedules and safety messages.

Commercial display or LED?

OptionBest for
Commercial LCD displayIndoor signage, menu boards, information screens
LED screen or video wallLarge formats, very bright areas, outdoor and shopfront displays

What to plan

  • Screen size and brightness for the viewing distance and light level.
  • Mounting, power and network at each screen.
  • Who updates content, and how (scheduled playlists, remote updates).
  • Support and replacement plans for screens in daily use.

faqs.q: Can I use a normal TV for digital signage?
faqs.a: For light use, sometimes. Commercial displays are built for long daily hours, higher brightness and portrait mounting, and usually carry a commercial warranty.

faqs.q: Can content be updated remotely across branches?
faqs.a: Yes. Networked media players let you schedule and update content for one screen or many locations from a central dashboard.

faqs.q: Do you install outdoor digital signage?
faqs.a: Yes, using weather-rated, high-brightness LED screens suitable for sun and rain.
